question_bank.question: When moving from the wake-word example to deep research, what system structure does the instructor introduce?
choices: A single end-to-end model whose internals should not be inspected separately.
A pipeline of components whose intermediate outputs can be checked and improved.
A collection of unrelated models where only the final answer is evaluated.
A fully manual workflow that avoids language models until the final report.
question_bank.explanation: The instructor introduces pipelines to describe systems made of stages, where the engineering problem includes deciding which component to improve.

source_ref.evidence_span: I'm going to use the term pipelines.

frame_evidence.description: Whiteboard shows a chain-like system diagram as the instructor transitions from one neural network to pipeline systems.

question_bank.question: In the simple deep-research pipeline drawn on the board, what happens immediately after the user query enters the system?
choices: The final article is written first so the search engine can verify it afterward.
The system selects final URLs before it knows what search terms to use.
An LLM generates search terms that are sent to a web search engine.
The system asks a human expert to label every retrieved page manually.
question_bank.explanation: The baseline pipeline begins by using an LLM to turn the query into search terms, which are then passed to web search.

source_ref.evidence_span: Use a large language model to generate search terms

frame_evidence.description: Whiteboard diagram shows query flowing into an LLM box and then toward search terms and web search.

question_bank.question: What capability distinguishes the more modern agentic deep-research versions from the simple linear pipeline?
choices: They can decide to loop back and gather more evidence before writing the final answer.
They avoid web search entirely and rely only on the model's pretrained memory.
They remove intermediate stages so there is no component-level bottleneck to analyze.
They replace the final writing stage with a fixed template that never changes.
question_bank.explanation: The instructor says newer systems are more autonomous and can go back for more pages or evidence, rather than always following one fixed pass.

source_ref.evidence_span: do I need to go back

frame_evidence.description: Whiteboard pipeline includes a multi-stage flow while the instructor discusses looping back for additional searches.

question_bank.question: Once an AI product is represented as a pipeline, what project-management question becomes central?
choices: Whether to train every stage end-to-end before inspecting any intermediate output.
Whether to remove the first stage because later language models can repair all mistakes.
Whether to evaluate only the final article because component errors are too subjective.
Which component should receive engineering attention first based on observed failures.
question_bank.explanation: Pipeline decomposition shifts the question from improving a vague system to identifying the stage whose failures most limit the final output.

source_ref.evidence_span: in the pipeline, which one do you want

frame_evidence.description: Instructor points along the board pipeline while asking which component should be improved next.
